searchText: With pytest, is there a way to match against a specific test case and combination of parameters? I'm guessing this involves formatting the value of `-k` correctly, but I can't figure out how. I want to run a single failing test-case/parameter combination I think so, and it uses square brackets. I can't remember more specifically than that 😅 ah. I tried messing around with the square brackets but haven't found the magic syntax to get it working. good to know that's the right direction though it will print out lines like this: ``` FAILED tests/cancun/eip6780_selfdestruct/test_selfdestruct.py::test_selfdestruct_pre_existing[fork=Shanghai-eip_enabled=True-pre_existing-selfdestruct_contract_initial_balance=100000-multiple_calls_multiple_sendall_recipients_including_self_different_order] - ... ``` And I try: ``` > ./venv/bin/fill -k 'test_selfdestruct_pre_existing[Shanghai-True-pre_existing-100000-multiple_calls_multiple_sendall_recipients_including_self_different_order]' ``` But it doesn't match anything . I always leave it out to vscode to deduce the command line for me 😂 But this is an example of what it comes up for a single test case: ``` pytest ./tests/cancun/eip5656_mcopy/test_mcopy.py::test_mcopy_on_empty_memory[fork=Cancun-empty_memory-length=0-src=0-dest=0] ``` So `<test file path>::<test function name>[<test parameters>]` `zsh: no matches found: ./tests/cancun/eip5656_mcopy/test_mcopy.py::test_mcopy_on_empty_memory[fork=Cancun-empty_memory-length=0-src=0-dest=0]` trying with bash different error: this time from pytest: `ERROR: file or directory not found: ./tests/cancun/eip5656_mcopy/test_mcopy.py::test_mcopy_on_empty_memory[fork=Cancun-empty_memory-length=0-src=0-dest=0]` oh that's because the specific command is something that's not the `main` branch no... I'm not on the main branch.. I'm on main yes 👍 This is the full command: ``` fill --until=Cancun './tests/cancun/eip5656_mcopy/test_mcopy.py::test_mcopy_on_empty_memory[fork=Cancun-empty_memory-length=0-src=0-dest=0]' ``` If you're not in the root `execution-spec-tests` folder, the path might need to be changed but it should work yup it works (and passes now that I am on the `main` branch 🙂 ). thanks If you're using vscode, I highly recommend setting up the `.vscode/settings.recommended.json`, it lists out the tests in the testing tab nicely and you can just pick any single one and run it very easily:

```
pytest ./tests/cancun/eip5656_mcopy/test_mcopy.py::test_mcopy_on_empty_memory[fork=Cancun-empty_memory-length=0-src=0-dest=0]
```

